correctness.rationale: The exact geometric-sum deficiency formula is independently checked against original sitewise detection by 51,980 rational cases. Strict convexity of the fixed-separation gap penalty proves centering for all n and q. Exponential defect bounds with balanced comparison prove thirds for each fixed q as n grows. Uniform finite-n q->1 expansions reduce to a discrete product-distance functional whose Riemann limit has unique quarter minimizers. Finite polynomial factor identities establish the sharp n=7 switching law; explicit signs and all boundaries are justified analytically. Exact verifier is supporting evidence, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Literature and semantic searches located the identical detection-kernel model from Dhillon et al. (2002) but a different minimum-sensors pointwise coverage criterion and heuristic. Sun et al. (2014) study estimation under a half-normal kernel; Frasca et al. (2014) analyze independent whole-sensor failures under a maximum-distance cost. The claimed exact two-trap average optimum, noncommuting thirds/quarters limits, and sharp n=7 switch are not implications of these inspected results; global bibliographic uniqueness remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact exponential-kernel two-detector result may exist in probabilistic facility location, gradual coverage or sensor design literature despite no match in searches.
A 2002 primary source has the same observation model, so the claim is only the stated optimum and scale noncommutation, not creation of the model.
The 2007 spatial capture–recapture article was consulted at abstract level only; source was not used to support a whole-document non-coverage conclusion.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural model-scale ambiguity in trap-spacing design: finite effective detection length on growing corridors selects thirds, while nearly uniform coverage at fixed corridor length selects quarters. The disagreement of iterated limits and sharp first small-size transition are nontrivial, motivated structural predictions, beyond a routine calculation at a single parameter. The objective and field-model limitations are stated explicitly.
